versos.texto_bv: Então contendeu o povo com Moisés, e disseram: Dê-nos água para beber. E Moisés lhes disse: Por que contendem comigo? Por que tentam ao SENHOR?
versos.traducao_literal: E contendeu o povo com Moisés, e disseram: Dai-nos água e beberemos. E disse a eles Moisés: Por que contendeis comigo? Por que tentais a YHWH?
objecoes: Objeção MATERIAL (revisão ER-0019): 'Dê-nos água' está no singular (você), mas o imperativo hebraico é 2ª pessoa do PLURAL; a norma exige preservar sempre a distinção singular/plural do original. Corrigir para 'Deem-nos' alteraria a estrutura de interlocução (quem é destinatário do pedido), o que ultrapassa a revisão de forma; o texto permanece inalterado. — evidência: termos_originais: תְּנוּ, lemma 5414, morfologia HVqv2mp; traducao_literal: 'Dai-nos água e beberemos'. Contraste: as falas de Moisés no mesmo verso vertem corretamente os plurais תְּרִיבוּן/תְּנַסּוּן (2mp) como 'contendem'/'tentam'.

kjv.texto: Wherefore the people did chide with Moses, and said, Give us water that we may drink. And Moses said unto them, Why chide ye with me? wherefore do ye tempt the Lord?

vizinhos.1: And all the congregation of the children of Israel journeyed from the wilderness of Sin, after their journeys, according to the commandment of the Lord, and pitched in Rephidim: and there was no water for the people to drink.
vizinhos.3: And the people thirsted there for water; and the people murmured against Moses, and said, Wherefore is this that thou hast brought us up out of Egypt, to kill us and our children and our cattle with thirst?

web.texto: Therefore the people quarreled with Moses, and said, “Give us water to drink.”   Moses said to them, “Why do you quarrel with me? Why do you test Yahweh?”

vizinhos.1: All the congregation of the children of Israel traveled from the wilderness of Sin, by their journeys, according to Yahweh’s commandment, and encamped in Rephidim; but there was no water for the people to drink.
vizinhos.3: The people were thirsty for water there; and the people murmured against Moses, and said, “Why have you brought us up out of Egypt, to kill us, our children, and our livestock with thirst?”
